Rating | Sampan Philly 🥡✨

Sampan isn’t one of Philly’s best happy hour spots for no reason. Not only do they have some of the best happy hour specials but also some amazing bites. My friends and I went for a girls’ night dinner and these are my thoughts.

Ambiance: The overall vibe was so tea. I’m convinced if Girlfriends were filmed in Philly, the girls would’ve easily frequented Sampan. It’s a perfect spot for grabbing drinks at the bar, or enjoying dinner with your girls or your boo.

Drinks: The drinks here did not disappoint. I am a sucker for a great espresso martini with reposado tequila. The girls that get it, get it. 💁🏾‍♀️ We each had 3 rounds and left feeling the perfect amount of tipsy to enjoy the rest of the evening. Enough said.

Appetizers: For me, the appetizers set the tone for the meal. Their appetizers actually carried the meal for us. Between the 5 of us we split a few different dishes and we did not have a single complaint. The crowd favorites being the wings and the dumplings. I can’t wait to go back for these two alone. They were sooo good!

Main course: Honestly, the main entrees let us down a little bit. The Szechuan chicken was our favorite of all of the dishes. However, the girls did not enjoy the sauce on the honey walnut shrimp because it had an unexpected mayo-based flavor. Likewise, the shrimp pad thai had an overpowering citrusy undertone due to the tamarind that we also didn’t care for very much. However, our server was accommodating and brought us substitutes with no fuss. 

Overall: I would highly recommend Sampan. We enjoyed our time here and will certainly make a point to go back. If you’re looking for a good place to go for dinner in Philly, centrally located next to a host of other cocktail bars, restaurants and vibes this is the spot for you!

You can tell this place is owned by the same owner as double knot. Similar ambiance, similar style with small plates, skewers, tasting menu etc. I think what stands out about Sampan in the Philly restaurant scene is their daily hh deals which would’ve been worth it. Unfortunately, for the amount of food we got vs price we paid we reallyyy should’ve done the tasting menu. Depends on personal preference tho bc I personally love to try as much as possible. 

Food specific: I got this short rib lo mein. I was debating between a few big plates and asked our server for her rec. Lowk this was a bit boring. Def yummy but def a safe option. Good flavors though and quality+ample meat. Would recommend if this is your thing.

DECEMBER 26-27 SNOW FORECAST

Another significant winter storm is on the way. Yet again, it’s a fast moving clipper that will track from northwest to southeast. It’s actually a fairly unconventional setup that typically is hostile for snow unless a storm is placed juuuust right.

We will see a collision of air masses as polar air from the northeast converges with mild air from the southwest. Not only does this lead to enhanced precipitation, it also means we’ll see an area of freezing rain and sleet.

I expect the most snow to fall roughly from Binghamton to Danbury where some could approach double digits. This is the sweet spot where we stay all snow, see rates of 1” per hour or greater, and have higher ratios.

Snow totals will rapidly decrease as one moves to the northeast due to dry air and to the southwest due to mixing. It will be a very NARROW corridor that sees heavy snow and can shift with adjustments to the track. I think the NYC Metro, including Long Island and down to I-195 is squarely within the zone for plowable snow while Philly, Albany, and Hartford likely just miss. 

I am also very concerned about a prolonged icing event across most of Pennsylvania, northern Maryland, northern Delaware, and southern New Jersey. We could see several hours of freezing rain and sleet.

Timing wise, this will be Friday evening to Saturday midday, worst overnight. Travel will be extremely treacherous if not impossible during this time.

Make sure to follow my page for additional updates on the storm!

Straight off their real-time coverage of the Fall of Crozer Health, cohosts of the award-winning 43cc podcast, Drs. Wendy Dean and Matt Ramsey, are hosting a live recording at the Pen and Pencil Club on Sunday, June 29 at 7:30 pm. Doors open at 7 pm.

43cc is an honest, fun, irreverent, and deadly serious podcast series that exposes the truth about healthcare (with a shot to dull the pain). Hosts Wendy Dean, M.D., and Matt Ramsey, M.D., take an in-depth look medicine’s machinery tearing the patient-physician relationship apart and how the medical community might stitch them back together.

At the P&P, Wendy and Matt will be talking about the stories both journalists and physicians carry, inviting the audience to join in, and reminding us why “together” is better.

Wendy Dean cofounded and leads Moral Injury of Healthcare, a 501c3 nonprofit, is the author of If I Betray These Words, and cohost of the Moral Matters and WCC podcasts. She practiced emergency medicine and psychiatry, spent a decade as a US Army civilian, deeply involved in medical innovation, and was an executive in a half-billion-dollar nonprofit. When the challenges of getting high quality healthcare nearly cost her physician husband his life, she left that work to change healthcare. She is now the leading voice for reframing health worker distress to include moral injury.

Dr. Matthew L. Ramsey is an orthopaedic surgeon subspecializing in shoulder and elbow surgery. Dr. Ramsey has held multiple leadership positions during his career as a board member, chief of service, Vice Chairman of the Department of Orthopaedic Surgery, and in subspecialty organizations and journals. He is committed to two ideals in reconstructive surgery of the shoulder and elbow: physician excellence and a holistic approach to patient care. He is passionate about preserving physician autonomy and physician leadership in healthcare.
